references.text: Moses brought forward the sin offering bull, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the bull's head—the same ritual described in the consecration ceremony in Exodus.
Describes what is to be done with the flesh, skin, and entrails of the sin offering bull—a continuation of the ritual that begins with the laying on of hands.
Basic instruction on laying hands on the head of the sin offering, which is the ritual Aaron and his sons perform here.
The elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the bull's head—the same principle of laying on of hands for a sin offering.
Laying hands on the head of the burnt offering to achieve atonement—a parallel ritual showing the significance of laying on of hands in the sacrificial system.
Aaron shall lay both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess the sins of Israel—laying on of hands as a symbol of the transfer of sin.
Christ did not need, like the Levitical high priests, to offer sacrifices first for his own sins—a contrast to Aaron's sin offering at consecration.
The blood of goats and bulls sanctified for fleshly purity, but Christ's blood cleanses the conscience—the typological fulfillment of the sin offering.
